# Cáishén and the industries that were always telling its story

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Cáishén** works now.

Cáishén's mythology is young and openly composite. The cult is a Song-dynasty growth over older roots, and every avatar brings his own story: a Ming novel supplies the marshal, a Han historian the heartless minister, merchants the retired sage. The tradition never pretends otherwise — and its honesty is part of its power.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **6 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Cáishén
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Domain of influence:** Wealth, Prosperity, New Year
- **Pattern seats:** 6
- **Sectors touched:** Commerce & Governance · Culture & Entertainment · Technology & Innovation · Society & Spirit
- **Strongest seat:** Finance, Wealth & Commerce
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 99 of 546

## The Myth at Work

**One Office, Many Gods.** The two characters 財神 simply mean 'god of wealth' — a title, not a personal name, and the tradition treats it that way.  There is no canonical birth-story of Cáishén; instead, the office has been filled, again and again, by figures the culture wished to honor: a loyal minister, a canonized marshal, an honest merchant, even the red-faced war-god Guan Yu in some regions. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**Zhao Gongming on the Black Tiger.** The fullest avatar-story comes from the Ming novel Fengshen Yanyi (Investiture of the Gods).  During the fall of the Shang dynasty, Zhao Gongming, a hermit of Mount Emei, comes down to aid the doomed house with his black tiger, his iron whip, and his magic pearls; battle after battle turns on his power, until Jiang Ziya's side breaks him with Lu Ya's sorcery — an effigy of straw pierced by arrows. — that is not just a story. It is a business model, four thousand years early.

## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Finance, Wealth & Commerce

*Banking, investment, and commercial enterprise. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*The Chinese god of wealth whose image appears in shops, homes, and businesses during the New Year.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Cáishén performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Mythic Name Restoration

*Scholarly Unicode restorations of mythic names for modern identity. (Sector: Culture & Entertainment)*

*The Chinese god of wealth in toned pinyin.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

## The Long Employment

At Lunar New Year, Cáishén is the busiest god alive.  The fifth-day welcome, the firecrackers, the reopened shops, the paper icons, and the greeting Gong Xi Fa Cai — 'wishing you prosperity' — all run on his calendar, from Harbin to Singapore to San Francisco. The age changed. The work did not.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

Skeptical? Good — the system is built for you. Every seat in this file carries its why-line and its weight, the full derivation is public at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/), and the challenge process is part of the design. Falsifiable is not a posture here; it is the mechanism.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in finance, wealth & commerce, mythic name restoration, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/caishen/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
